trials.name: Observational Study on Immunoadsorption (IA) in Patients With Autoantibody-Positive Post-Infectious ME/CFS

intervention.name: Immunoadsorption (TheraSorb®)
intervention.mechanism: Removes GPCR autoantibodies (adrenergic, antineuronal) from blood via TheraSorb® affinity column (Miltenyi); 5 outpatient sessions over 2 weeks.

trials.sponsor: Charité University, Berlin (supported by German Federal Ministry of Research and Weidenhammer-Zöbele Foundation)

sites.institution: Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Institute for Medical Immunology

eligibility.summary: Adults 18–65 with post-infectious ME/CFS (Canadian Consensus Criteria), Bell Disability Score <60, post-exertional malaise ≥14 h, and detectable autoantibodies (adrenergic or antineuronal).
key_inclusion: ME/CFS per Canadian Consensus Criteria with PEM ≥14 h
key_exclusion: Conditions that preclude definite ME/CFS diagnosis

trials.name: Randomized Adaptive Assessment of Post-COVID Syndrome Treatments — REVIVE arm (vidofludimus calcium)

intervention.name: Vidofludimus calcium (IMU-838)
intervention.mechanism: Oral selective DHODH inhibitor with anti-inflammatory and antiviral activity (also activates the neuroprotective transcription factor Nurr1). Dosing 22.5 mg/day for 7 days, then 45 mg/day for 49 days, vs placebo. Rationale: reduce inflammatory activity in Post-COVID Syndrome.

trials.sponsor: Goethe University Frankfurt (Prof. Dr. Maria J. G. T. Vehreschild); part of the NAPKON / Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin (NUM) post-COVID platform, BMBF-funded, co-financed by a pharmaceutical manufacturer.
trials.principal_investigator: Prof. Dr. Maria J. G. T. Vehreschild (Infectiology, University Hospital Frankfurt); trial coordination University Medical Center Göttingen
trials.condition: Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) with moderate–severe disability — overlaps the post-COVID ME/CFS population (fatigue, PEM-adjacent exertional intolerance, cognitive and orthostatic symptoms)
trials.phase: Phase 2 (double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1 response-adaptive randomised platform arm; n≈376 across 11 German sites)

eligibility.summary: Adults ≥18 with Post-COVID Syndrome persisting >12 weeks after COVID-19, moderate–severe disability (Bell Disability Scale 20–60), and ≥2 PCS symptoms of moderate/severe intensity (e.g. fatigue FSS ≥36, cognitive impairment MoCA 10–25, dyspnea mMRC ≥2, or orthostatic dysfunction).
key_inclusion: Post-COVID Syndrome symptoms persisting >12 weeks after COVID-19
≥2 PCS symptoms incl. fatigue (FSS ≥36), cognitive impairment (MoCA 10–25), dyspnea (mMRC ≥2), or orthostatic dysfunction

trials.notes: Added 2026-06-30 after this trial was found to have been missed by earlier runs. ROOT CAUSE of the miss: registry searches used only ME/CFS-specific terms (ME/CFS, chronisches Fatigue-Syndrom, myalgische Enzephalomyelitis, post-exertional) and never 'Post-COVID-Syndrom'/'Long COVID', and the NAPKON/NUM post-COVID platform was not a monitored source — so a post-COVID drug RCT (even one with a Charité site) was invisible. Targets PCS broadly, not ME/CFS-exclusively, but eligibility (Bell 20–60, fatigue/PEM-adjacent, orthostatic) heavily overlaps post-COVID ME/CFS, which is explicitly in scope. RAPID is the adaptive platform; REVIVE is its first intervention-specific arm ('reducing inflammatory activity in PCS'). Confirmed via CTIS 2024-511628-16-00 and the published protocol (PMC12366011); first patient enrolled Sep 2024; ~376 patients, 11 German sites incl. Charité Berlin (Prof. Witzenrath). Not a Wirth/Scheibenbogen trial (priority normal). STATUS CHANGE 2026-07-02: CTIS record itself still not directly fetchable (SPA, blocked), but the dedicated NAPKON institutional page (https://www.netzwerk-universitaetsmedizin.de/forschung/napkon-tip/studie-rapid-revive, 'Stand: Juli 2025') now states enrollment is full at all sites and no further recruitment is possible ('Es wurden bereits so viele Patient:innen an allen Standorten in die Studie eingeschlossen, dass derzeit keine weiteren rekrutiert werden können'), corroborated by a March 24, 2025 NUM news item (>100 of a planned 150 patients enrolled) and a Feb 9, 2026 Universitätsmedizin Halle NUM-Insights event titled 'Erste Ergebnisse aus RAPID_REVIVE' presented by Prof. Vehreschild, indicating the trial has moved into results/analysis. Status changed from recruiting to active_not_recruiting (enrollment complete, results pending); no longer open for enrollment. Recommend a follow-up attempt at the formal CTIS record next cycle to get the official EU status label. Re-confirmed 2026-07-03: still active_not_recruiting. Formal CTIS portal remains unfetchable (JS-shell/403), but an institutional site page for one of the 11 sites (Klinikum Lippe, https://www.klinikum-lippe.de/klinische-studien/post-covid-syndrom/) now explicitly states 'Rekrutierung abgeschlossen' (recruitment completed), corroborating the closed status. Re-confirmed 2026-07-04: still active_not_recruiting; NAPKON institutional page (Stand Juli 2025) unchanged, still states enrollment is full at all sites. Formal CTIS record (2024-511628-16-00) still returns only the static EMA page shell, no fetchable trial data — status label unconfirmed via CTIS itself for the fourth consecutive check. Re-confirmed 2026-07-05: still active_not_recruiting, independently corroborated by the German ME/CFS Society's therapy overview page (mecfs.de/therapie-von-me-cfs/) describing the trial as fully recruited (376 patients, 11 NAPKON sites). Formal CTIS record still unfetchable (EMA page shell only) — status label unconfirmed via CTIS itself for the fifth consecutive check. STATUS CHANGE 2026-07-06: the formal CTIS record became fetchable for the first time via its public JSON API (https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api/retrieve/2024-511628-16-00 — the human-readable /ctis-public/view/ page is still a JS shell, but the underlying API endpoint returned full data). It shows ctStatus 'Ended', recruitment 2024-08-27 to 2025-07-04 (376 subjects across 10 German sites, target met), a temporary halt from 2025-07-04, and formal early termination on 2025-09-30 with reason 'Sponsor Decision' (classified as a 'late candidate' for early termination — plausibly tied to the RAPID adaptive platform's planned Day-56/iDMC analysis checkpoint for the first 150 patients, not necessarily a safety failure). Status upgraded from active_not_recruiting to terminated to reflect this authoritative registry confirmation; last_status_change backdated to the real-world CTIS event date (2025-09-30) now that it's known, superseding the earlier discovery-date-based active_not_recruiting entry. trials.name: Randomized Adaptive Assessment of Post-COVID Syndrome Treatments — ELAPSE sub-protocol (bupropion)

intervention.name: Bupropion
intervention.mechanism: Already-approved dopamine/noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (antidepressant / smoking-cessation drug) repurposed for Post-COVID fatigue; 300 mg/day oral for 56 days vs placebo.

trials.sponsor: Goethe-Universität Frankfurt (Prof. Dr. Maria Vehreschild); RAPID adaptive platform, Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin (NUM), BMBF/BMFTR-funded
trials.principal_investigator: Coordinating study center: Universitätsmedizin Göttingen; RAPID master-protocol lead Prof. Dr. Maria Vehreschild

sites.institution: Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Campus Benjamin Franklin (Psychiatry)

trials.condition: Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) with fatigue as the primary feature — overlaps post-COVID ME/CFS (PEM-adjacent)

eligibility.summary: Adults ≥18 with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection ≥3 months prior, fatigue plus at least one of dyspnea/breathlessness, reduced physical exercise capacity, cognitive impairment, post-exertional malaise (PEM), or moderate-to-severe physical impairment; symptoms ≥3 months with no better alternative diagnosis.
key_inclusion: Fatigue plus ≥1 of: dyspnea/breathlessness, reduced exercise capacity, cognitive impairment, post-exertional malaise (PEM), or moderate-to-severe physical impairment
Symptoms persisting ≥3 months with no better alternative diagnosis

trials.notes: New trial found 2026-08-15: successor sub-protocol to the terminated rapid-revive (RAPID_REVIVE) arm, under the same RAPID adaptive-platform master protocol (NAPKON/Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin, sponsor Goethe-Universität Frankfurt/Prof. Maria Vehreschild). trials.name: Prospective, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Phase 2b Trial Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of the Anti-CD19 Monoclonal Antibody Inebilizumab Compared With Placebo in Patients With Post-acute Infection Syndromes Fulfilling ME/CFS Criteria

intervention.name: Inebilizumab (Uplizna®)
intervention.mechanism: Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibody depleting B cells (incl. antibody-producing plasmablasts); 300 mg IV on Day 1, Day 15, and Week 24, with premedication (methylprednisolone, dimetindene, paracetamol), vs. saline placebo on the same schedule.

trials.sponsor: Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin (NKSG-2 programme, BMFTR-funded award 01EP2601, €7,999,049 for 2026–2029)
trials.principal_investigator: Dr. Judith Bellmann-Strobl, MD (Senior Physician, Charité)
trials.condition: Post-acute infection syndrome (PAIS) fulfilling ME/CFS criteria (incl. post-COVID), elevated β2-adrenergic-receptor autoantibodies, prior immunoadsorption responders who later relapsed

eligibility.summary: Adults 18–65 with PAIS/ME/CFS (Canadian Consensus Criteria, PEM >14h), Bell Disability Score 30–60, documented β2-adrenergic-receptor autoantibodies, prior immunoadsorption with a clinical response (≥10-point SF-36 Physical Function increase at week 8) followed by worsening (≥10-point decrease for ≥3 months).
key_inclusion: PAIS diagnosis with ME/CFS per Canadian Consensus Criteria, PEM >14 hours
Prior immunoadsorption ≥6 months before enrollment, with initial response then relapse
key_exclusion: Immunomodulatory therapy within 3 months before screening
Significant hepatic, renal, or hematologic abnormalities

trials.name: Prospective, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Phase 2b Trial of Low-dose Aripiprazole in Patients With Neuropsychiatric Impairment in Post-acute Infectious Syndrome (PAIS)

intervention.name: Low-dose aripiprazole
intervention.mechanism: Dopamine D2/serotonin 5-HT1A partial agonist, used off-label at low dose in prior retrospective ME/CFS case series; 1 mg tablet every other day for 2 weeks, then once daily for 6 weeks per treatment period, vs placebo.

trials.condition: Post-acute infection syndrome (PAIS) / Long COVID with neuropsychiatric symptoms and fatigue; ME/CFS assessed as a secondary subgroup (not required for enrollment)

eligibility.summary: Adults ≥18 with confirmed/suspected prior infection and PAIS/post-COVID-19 condition symptoms ≥3 months, self-reported neuropsychiatric symptoms at screening, Bell Disability Scale ≥30 (excluded if <30).
key_inclusion: History of confirmed or suspected infectious disease
key_exclusion: Prior chronic neuroimmunological or neurodegenerative disease
Severe psychiatric disease within the last 10 years

trials.notes: Included per the post-COVID triage rule in sources/search-sources.md: drug intervention + eligibility gated on a Bell Disability Scale cutoff (≥30) capturing the ME/CFS-overlapping fatigue/functional-impairment phenotype, even though enrollment doesn't require a formal ME/CFS diagnosis or Canadian Consensus Criteria (ME/CFS is assessed as a secondary subgroup). Likely — but not certainly — the registered form of the previously-tracked 'PAIS-AriLis' Medscape lead (planned aripiprazole + lisdexamfetamine combination for neuropsychiatric PAIS): the registered design here is aripiprazole monotherapy, so treat as a probable but unconfirmed 1:1 continuation of that lead. First posted on ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-07-20, confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-07-30.
